# Week 4: Sustainable Growth
## Rooted Stewardship — Not Self-Hatred Agriculture

> **Week 4 of 4** | 9–11 hours | Capstone  
> **Sources:** Weeks 1–3 · Course 05 Laws · Course 07 MDS · plant analogy · Hebrews 5:14

---

## The Central Truth

Growth is sustainable when rooted in design, not in self-hatred.  
A plant grows steady, healthy, rooted. Scorched-earth “improvement” kills the life it claims to cultivate. You remain teleios by design; growth is likeness over Law of Time and Repetition — not a project to finally become human.

---

## Week Overview

### Core Question
How do we grow without punishing ourselves into change?

### Key Insight
Audit growth patterns: which are stewardship, which are self-punishment costume? Replace punishment with rails + a 30-day goal that assumes Week 1 ontology. Launch the log. Write the Perfect Self closing charter that locks Courses 11’s grammar for the rest of School 1’s finale (12–13).

### Learning Outcomes
By the end of this week you will:

- Audit growth patterns (stewardship vs punishment)
- Install a miss protocol that refuses multi-day identity sentences
- Set one 30-day design-rooted growth goal with a visible metric
- Launch Days 1–7 of the 30-day growth log
- Write a Perfect Self closing charter (witnessed)

---

## Core Teaching

### 1) Pattern audit

| Pattern I use | Stewardship? | Punishment? | Keep / Replace | Why |
|---------------|--------------|-------------|----------------|-----|
| Extreme challenges after shame | | | | |
| Public declarations without rails | | | | |
| Silent self-contempt | | | | |
| MDS + repair (Course 07) | | | | |
| Joy ritual (Week 3) | | | | |

Be ruthless. “High standards” that require self-hatred are still illegal.

### 2) Self-stewardship rule (non-negotiable)

After miss:

1. Own the act (specific)  
2. Repair within the time you promised (same day when possible)  
3. Resume the rail next cue  
4. No multi-day sentence  
5. No identity deletion  
6. Optional: one witness check if the miss is patterned  

This is holiness with Behavioral teeth — not soft denial.

### 3) 30-day goal — design-rooted

Rules for the goal:

- One domain only (speech, sleep, desire loyalty, presence, money order, etc.)  
- Metric visible to you (and ideally a witness)  
- Weekly 15-minute review  
- Ontology line fixed in writing: “I grow as teleios, not into personhood.”  
- Fatigue-ready minimum (MDS logic)

Illegal goals: “become a new me”; “earn the right to be loved”; “finally be enough.”

### 4) Growth log (30 days; launch now)

| Day | Rail / metric | Kept? | Miss? | Repair within window? | Chase grammar noticed? | Note |
|-----|---------------|-------|-------|------------------------|------------------------|------|

Days 1–7 are this week’s assignment; Days 8–30 continue after Course 11 closes.

### 5) Analogy: plant

Water, light, soil, time.  
Not ripping the plant up daily to check roots.  
Not bleaching the plant to force “purity.”  
Not refusing water because “I should already be a forest.”

Law of Time (Course 05): depth needs duration.  
Law of Repetition: reps stabilize.  
Neither invents ontology.

### 6) Hebrews 5:14 — again

Senses exercised in the life of the mature — responsibility profile, not maturity factory. Sustainable growth is exercised discernment and practice as a teleios person under load.

### 7) Integration map (Course 11)

| Week | Install |
|------|---------|
| 1 | Teleios starting point |
| 2 | Identity practice / mirror rails |
| 3 | Holiness & joy (state + sunlight) |
| 4 | Sustainable growth (plant + 30-day) |

Remove Week 1 and the rest becomes chase with better tools.

### 8) Continuity into Course 12

Emotional Literacy will train naming and governance of feeling. If chase returns (“I am my emotions” or “I must feel holy”), you will fail literacy. Carry the declaration into Week 1 of Course 12 explicitly.

### 9) Better whole

Do not make a spouse the scorekeeper of your 30-day goal in a parental way. Witness ≠ parent. Adult stewardship invites accountability without fusion.

### 10) Final ratiocination

- Premise 1: Teleios persons still require likeness over time.
- Premise 2: Self-hatred agriculture damages persons and households.
- Premise 3: Rails + repair + joy + duration produce sustainable fruit.
- Conclusion: Growth is stewardship of design — or it is not growth worthy of School 1.

---

### 11) Linking the 30-day goal to School 1 rails you already own

Do not invent a exotic goal. Prefer a goal that reactivates an existing rail:

- Course 07 MDS item that drifted
- Course 10 rulebook rule that became a wish again
- Course 11 identity practice cue
- Course 08 repair speed

Sustainable growth often means **returning** to design you already named — under Law of Time — not collecting new certificates.

### 12) Pride risk after “I practice from perfection”

Teleios grammar can be twisted into superiority over “less mature” people. Illegal. Ontology is gift. Likeness is responsibility. If your 30-day plan includes contempt for others’ pace, rewrite the plan.

### 13) Sample 30-day goal (template only)

Domain: evening presence.  
Metric: device-free 20 minutes with spouse/friend/family ≥5 nights/week.  
Miss protocol: same-night ownership + make-up block within 24h.  
Weekly review: Sunday 15 minutes with witness.  
Ontology line: “I am teleios; this is likeness, not worth purchase.”

Rewrite to your domain; keep the structure.

### 14) Anti-scorch inventory (replace these)

| Scorched pattern | Stewardship replacement |
|------------------|-------------------------|
| 30-day extreme after shame spike | MDS-sized goal, fatigue-ready |
| Public announcement, private abandon | Witnessed quiet log |
| Multi-day identity funeral after miss | Same-window repair + resume |
| “New me Monday” forever | Continue count with honesty |
| Using spouse as warden | Adult witness, not parent |

### 15) Charter must-include lines (Course 11)

Your closing charter is incomplete unless it contains:

1. Teleios starting-point sentence
2. Two retired chase finish lines
3. Identity practice cue
4. Joy ritual cue
5. 30-day goal + miss protocol
6. How you will refuse chase in Courses 12–13 by name

### 16) Depth standard

School 1 greatness is not more content modules. It is graduates who grow like plants — rooted, timed, joyful — not like arsonists of their own souls. Write the charter accordingly.

### 17) Thirty-day review agenda (copy into calendar)

Week 1 check: ontology language still clean?  
Week 2 check: identity practice cue firing?  
Week 3 check: joy ritual not chase?  
Week 4 check: miss protocol used without funerals?  
Adjust metric once if needed — do not restart identity.

### 18) Final charge

Do not leave Course 11 entertained. Leave planted. Water the 30-day goal. Keep the joy ritual. Interrupt chase speech. School 1's reputation in your home begins with whether perfection remains a starting point when you fail on Day 11.

## Diagnostic — Sustainable Growth Audit

Score 1–5.

| Statement | Score |
|-----------|-------|
| Growth patterns audited honestly | |
| Punishment patterns named for replacement | |
| Miss protocol written | |
| 30-day goal is design-rooted (not “new me”) | |
| Log launched with Days 1–7 | |
| Weekly review scheduled | |
| Teleios remains starting point in my speech | |
| I refuse scorched-earth challenges as identity | |

---

## Case Contrasts

### Case A — Scorched growth
Avery burns through 75-hard clones after every shame spike, quits by Day 12, concludes she is hopeless. Self-hatred fertilizer. Soil dies.

### Case B — No growth
Morgan rests in teleios talk, skips rails, calls drift “resting in identity.” Ontology without likeness. Weeds.

### Case C — Planted
Sam sets one 30-day presence/sleep goal, miss-repairs Day 6 in hours, keeps joy ritual, reviews Sunday with witness, speech still says “I am teleios; I steward.” Fruit begins quietly.

---

## Seven-Day Drill — Capstone Launch

**Day 1:** Pattern audit + miss protocol.  
**Day 2:** 30-day goal written + metric + review calendar.  
**Days 3–7:** Growth log; joy ritual continues; identity practice continues.  
**Day 7:** Closing charter + witness.

---

---

## Course 01 parity — School 1 greatness evidence bar

Capstone evidence: 30-day sustainable growth plan with one rail per faculty/attribute band, witness review, chase relapse plan, and explicit bridge to Course 12 without pride. Sustainable growth that increases contempt or secrecy failed Course 11 — regardless of page count.

### Integration — School 1 capstone band (11–13)

Course 12 names and mends emotion; Course 13 honors temperament. Week 4 here seals **teleios practice** so the band does not become three self-help electives. Course 01 parity: greatness is kitchen fruit for 90 days — not LMS completion pride.

### Formation under load — Tuesday test
### Additional formation depth — Course 01 standard

School 1 greatness is not measured by reading completion. It is measured when a household can feel the rails: faster repair, cleaner speech, governed emotion, honored difference, and practice that starts from teleios rather than chasing worth. This week’s assignment must produce **observable fruit** — a log, a witness, a kept act, a retired phrase — not only insight.

Write one paragraph answering: *What would my closest relationship experience if I kept this week’s rule for 30 days?* If the answer is “nothing different,” the rule is too vague. Sharpen until the household would feel it.

Carry Course 01 integration forward: formation is structural; information is cosmetic. A great week leaves evidence in time, speech, and body — not only in notes.


Your 30-day plan must include repair speed and emotional naming — or Course 12 will be theory on arrival.

### Parity seal

This week meets Course 01 depth when your witness can describe one visible change in your speech, schedule, or repair — without you prompting them. If they cannot, extend the week. School 1 does not graduate fog.

## Reflection Questions

1. Which “growth” habit is actually punishment?
2. What 30-day goal is small enough to keep on your worst days?
3. How will you treat a Day-10 miss without identity collapse?
4. What does rooted look like in your household’s experience of you?
5. What charter line must never be renegotiated when Course 12–13 get hard?
6. How does Law of Time confront your addiction to dramatic restarts?

---

## Weekly Assignment

1. Sustainable Growth Audit  
2. Pattern audit sheet  
3. Written miss protocol  
4. 30-day goal (metric + review)  
5. Growth log Days 1–7 (and calendar for 8–30)  
6. Perfect Self closing charter (700–1000 words) integrating Weeks 1–4 and naming how you will refuse chase in Courses 12–13

---

## Closing Declaration

> Growth is stewardship.  
> I refuse self-hatred as fertilizer.  
> Teleios is my starting point.  
> Thirty days — rooted, joyful, true.  
> Practice from perfection — then keep practicing.

---

## Outcome

You complete Course 11 with a 30-day design-rooted growth plan, a miss protocol, and a charter that locks practice-from-teleios as School 1’s finishing grammar.
reflection_questions: Which “growth” habit is actually punishment?
What 30-day goal is small enough to keep?
How will you treat Day-10 miss?
What does rooted look like in your household?
What charter line must never be renegotiated?

modules.content:
# Week 1: Naming Emotions
## Label the Jars — Clarity Brings Order

> **Week 1 of 4** | 8–10 hours | Emotional Vocabulary  
> **Sources:** Course 06 W4 · Course 10 W3 · Course 11 · Course 04 (Affective ≠ Emotional) · better whole

---

## The Central Truth

You cannot govern what you cannot name.  
Labeling jars brings order to a pantry; unnamed feelings become anonymous tyrants. Emotional literacy begins with honest vocabulary — for couples and for singles practicing covenant readiness — without baptizing feelings as ontology (“I am my anger”) and without chasing worth through emotional performance (Course 11).

---

## Week Overview

### Core Question
How does naming restore capacity to steward emotion as a teleios person?

### Key Insight
People hide “unacceptable” emotions (anger, envy, fear, desire, contempt, tenderness) and then leak them sideways. Name ten from this week; note which you hide; practice daily naming as Mental clarity + Emotional attribute stewardship — not as dumping, and not as identity.

### Learning Outcomes
By the end of this week you will:

- Distinguish Emotional attribute from Affective faculty in plain speech
- List 10 emotions with precision (beyond mad/sad/fine)
- Identify hidden emotions and their leak routes
- Keep a 7-day emotion log with intensity and cues
- Pass a Naming Emotions Audit without fine-culture fog

---

## Core Teaching

### 1) Attribute vs faculty (doctrine lock)

| | Meaning in this canon |
|--|------------------------|
| **Emotional attribute** | How feeling states move, intensify, and get governed in the person |
| **Affective faculty** | Capacity to care, value, attach with forethought |

Literacy trains the **attribute** (name and govern feeling). It does not replace Affective care. Collapsing them produces either cold technique or unmanaged care floods.

### 2) Why naming matters (ratiocination)

- Premise 1: Ungoverned emotion still acts (Behavioral leak).
- Premise 2: What is unnamed tends to fuse with identity or hide until ambush.
- Premise 3: Teleios persons remain responsible for speech and acts under feeling (Course 07 / 11).
- Conclusion: Naming is the first stewardship move — epistemic clarity for Conative choice.

### 3) Expand vocabulary (precision reduces explosion)

Beyond mad/sad/fine: frustrated, grieved, envious, ashamed, delighted, tender, lonely, hopeful, contemptuous, peaceful, anxious, jealous, grateful, resentful, eager, overwhelmed, secure, discarded (feeling — not ontology).

Precision is honor. Vague “upset” often hides contempt or fear.

### 4) Hide inventory

Which emotions felt “illegal” in your family, church, gender scripts, or marriage?  
Hiding trains ambush: sarcasm, stonewall, illness theater, pornographic escape, spending, spiritualizing.

Write three hidden emotions + their usual leak route.

### 5) Naming ≠ dumping; naming ≠ fusion

| Healthy naming | Dumping | Fusion |
|----------------|---------|--------|
| “I feel X about Y” | Flood to control | “I am X; fix me” |
| Time-bound | No return | Partner as regulator |
| Invites understanding | Demands absorption | Better-half medicine |

### 6) Emotion log (7 days)

| Time | Emotion word | Intensity 1–5 | Cue | Body | Hidden? | Leak risk |
|------|--------------|---------------|-----|------|---------|-----------|

Morning scan + evening scan minimum.

### 7) Couples and singles tracks

**Couples:** Share one named emotion daily **without fixing** for 3 minutes. Mirror once (Course 10 W4). No advice unless asked.

**Singles:** Name without recruiting a fantasy partner as witness. Journal + one wise friend. Literacy is readiness practice, not a waiting-room identity.

### 8) Analogy: labeled jars

Unlabeled spices ruin the meal. Unlabeled feelings ruin the conversation and the conscience. Labels do not invent the spice; they make cooking possible.

### 9) Course 11 guard

If naming becomes chase (“I must feel the right feelings to be okay”), stop and return to teleios declaration. Feelings report; they do not mint worth.

### 10) Continuity into Week 2

Named emotion still needs a brake. Week 2 installs regulation — active control between feeling and act.

---

### 11) A starter lexicon (use and add)

Anger family: irritated, frustrated, furious, resentful, bitter, contemptuous.  
Fear family: uneasy, anxious, panicked, dread, insecure.  
Sadness family: down, grieved, lonely, disappointed, hopeless (feeling — not ontology).  
Shame family: embarrassed, humiliated, guilty (act-focused) vs worthless (illegal ontology).  
Gladness family: glad, grateful, delighted, peaceful, hopeful, tender.

For three hidden emotions, write: word · body · cue · what I usually do · design alternative.

### 12) Children / household modeling

If you parent or influence younger people: fine-culture trains them to hide. Naming without dumping models literacy. “I feel frustrated about the mess; I will ask for help” beats silent rage or fog.

### 13) Ratiocination for couples’ nightly share

- Premise 1: Unshared emotion becomes leak or explosion.
- Premise 2: Fixing mid-share trains the speaker to stop naming.
- Premise 3: Mirror listening (Course 10) + time-box protects both.
- Conclusion: Three minutes of named emotion without fixing is literacy practice, not therapy theater.

Script for the listener: paraphrase once; ask “do you want comfort, help, or just witness?”; obey the answer.

### 14) What “good enough for School 1” requires this week

Not poetic feelings essays. A log with precise words, hidden emotions confessed, and at least three shared namings. If you cannot produce the log, you are not ready to claim literacy — return to Week 1 until the jars are labeled.

### 15) Mapping body to word (literacy laboratory)

For five days, when intensity ≥3, complete:

1. Body location (chest, gut, jaw, hands, heat)
2. First imprecise word (“bad / weird / upset”)
3. Precise word from lexicon
4. Need underneath (comfort, justice, rest, boundary, repentance, help)
5. One sentence you could say without dumping

This trains Cognitive precision under Emotional load — the heart of literacy.

### 16) Illegal namings (still name the feeling; fix the ontology)

- “I am anxiety” → “I feel anxious about ______.”
- “I am worthless” → “I feel ashamed about ______ act.”
- “I am my rage” → “I feel furious about ______; I will govern the act.”

Course 11 grammar inside Course 12 vocabulary.

### 17) Couples: the no-fix covenant (write and sign)

> For three minutes after an emotion is named, I will not advise, defend, or problem-solve unless asked. I will mirror once. I will ask comfort / help / witness.

Break the covenant → repair using Course 12 Week 4 early.

### 18) Singles track — loneliness without fusion fantasy

Loneliness is a real emotion word. Illegal move: using fantasy romance as the only witness. Legal move: name lonely; journal; call a real friend; refuse “I am incomplete” ontology. Literacy prepares covenant; it does not postpone honesty until a wedding.

### 19) Depth bar for Week 1 completion

You are not done when you "understand" naming. You are done when the 7-day log exists, three shares happened, hide inventory is written, and you can explain Emotional attribute vs Affective faculty to a witness in under two minutes without notes.

### 20) Teleios + better whole (naming edition)

You are teleios by design. Naming feelings does not invent a self and does not mint worth (Course 11). Feelings report; they do not rule; they do not rewrite ontology.

Better whole: a partner is not a permanent jar-labeler or emotional regulator. Couples share naming; each person still owns their Emotional attribute. Singles refuse fantasy partners as the only witness to interior life.

Illegal: “I am my anger / envy / anxiety.”  
Legal: “I feel ______ about ______; I remain teleios; I will govern the next act.”

### 21) Loop preview

Course 12 loop: **name → regulate → conflict tools → repair.** Week 1 is only the first hinge. Vocabulary without Weeks 2–4 becomes either fine-culture relapse or dumping theater.

---

## Diagnostic — Naming Emotions Audit

Score 1–5.

| Statement | Score |
|-----------|-------|
| I can separate Emotional attribute from Affective faculty | |
| I listed 10 precise emotion words from this week | |
| Hidden emotions and leak routes named | |
| 7-day log completed | |
| I refuse fine-only vocabulary | |
| Naming is not dumping | |
| I refuse “I am my feeling” ontology | |
| Couples/singles practice done without fusion | |

---

## Case Contrasts

### Case A — Fine culture
Avery only says fine; home walks on eggshells; contempt leaks as “jokes.” No jars labeled; pantry on fire.

### Case B — Flood naming
Riley names constantly to overwhelm and avoid responsibility. Vocabulary as weapon. Partner becomes container.

### Case C — Literacy
Sam logs precisely, shares one clean sentence with spouse/friend, refuses fix-it mode, notices envy without becoming “I am envy,” and prepares Week 2 pause.

---

## Seven-Day Drill

**Day 1:** Vocabulary expansion sheet + hide inventory.  
**Days 2–7:** Full emotion log; one shared naming (couple or witness) on at least three days.

---

---

## Course 01 parity — School 1 greatness evidence bar

Show: lexicon growth (≥12 precise words used live), illegal emotion audit, one naming conversation that did not immediately fix, and Course 11 teleios sentence preserved (“feeling is signal, not ontology”). Naming without precision is venting with vocabulary — not literacy.

### Integration — Course 02 attributes + Course 11

Emotional attribute sits inside personal development; it is not identity. Course 11 forbids feeling-as-ontology. Week 1 builds the **word bank** Course 12 Weeks 2–4 will govern and mend.

### Formation under load — Tuesday test
### Additional formation depth — Course 01 standard

School 1 greatness is not measured by reading completion. It is measured when a household can feel the rails: faster repair, cleaner speech, governed emotion, honored difference, and practice that starts from teleios rather than chasing worth. This week’s assignment must produce **observable fruit** — a log, a witness, a kept act, a retired phrase — not only insight.

Write one paragraph answering: *What would my closest relationship experience if I kept this week’s rule for 30 days?* If the answer is “nothing different,” the rule is too vague. Sharpen until the household would feel it.

Carry Course 01 integration forward: formation is structural; information is cosmetic. A great week leaves evidence in time, speech, and body — not only in notes.


Name the emotion aloud in your highest-risk cue this week. Private naming only is halfway literacy.

## Reflection Questions

1. Which emotion is most “illegal” in your story — and who taught that?
2. What do you lose by staying at “fine”?
3. How does naming protect better whole?
4. Couples: what happens when you name without fixing?
5. Singles: where does fantasy replace honest naming?
6. Where have you used emotion words to dodge a Behavioral next act?

---

## Weekly Assignment

1. Naming Emotions Audit  
2. Ten-emotion list with definitions in your own words  
3. Hide inventory + leak routes  
4. 7-day emotion log  
5. Shared naming practice notes (3+ days)  
6. 400–600 words: “What I refuse to feel — and what it costs”

---

## Closing Declaration

> I name what I feel.  
> Naming is the start of governance.  
> I refuse anonymous tyranny and feeling-as-ontology.  
> Clarity brings order.  
> I am teleios — feelings report; they do not rule.

---

## Outcome

You build emotional vocabulary with a week of labeled evidence — literacy’s first jar labels, doctrine-locked to teleios stewardship.
reflection_questions: Which emotion is most illegal in your story?
What do you lose by staying at “fine”?
How does naming protect better whole?
Couples: what happens when you name without fixing?
What word was hardest to admit?

modules.title: Regulation
modules.content:
# Week 2: Regulation
## Brake Pedal — Control Is Active

> **Week 2 of 4** | 8–10 hours | Feeling → Governed Action  
> **Sources:** Week 1 · Course 07 impulse · Course 10 W3 · Proverbs 16:32 · better whole

---

## The Central Truth

Regulation is the bridge between feeling and action.  
A brake pedal is active control — not the absence of a car, and not the killing of the engine. You feel; you choose the next act under design. Chaos is not honesty. Numbness is not holiness. Proverbs 16:32 ranks rule of spirit above city-taking bravado — inner command outranks outer conquest.

---

## Week Overview

### Core Question
How do we move from named feeling to governed response without freeze or explosion?

### Key Insight
Triggers are predictable. A pause practice turns weather into navigation. Replace reaction with response in a 5-day pause-before-act challenge — under real load, not classroom calm.

### Learning Outcomes
By the end of this week you will:

- Map triggers with body / premise / urge / usual act
- Write a 60–90 second pause practice card
- Complete a 5-day pause-before-act challenge with honest miss logging
- Distinguish regulation from freeze and from suppression-as-virtue
- Pass a Regulation Audit

---

## Core Teaching

### 1) The chain (literacy version)

Trigger → Sensation → Premise (Mental) → Emotion named (Week 1) → Urge peak → Act / Pause → Response

Interrupt points: premise, peak, act. Literacy without interrupt is vocabulary for postmortems only.

### 2) Pause practice (under 90 seconds)

1. Stop the Behavioral launch (mouth, send, spend, exit without return)  
2. Breathe / ground (Psychomotor)  
3. Name the emotion word (Week 1)  
4. Test premise: design-aligned or illegal story?  
5. Choose one governed next act (or scheduled pause with return time)  
6. Log one line  

No debate club at peak. Decide after pause.

### 3) Regulation ≠ freeze ≠ numbness

| Regulation | Freeze | Numbness theater |
|------------|--------|------------------|
| Feel + choose | Feel + stuck | Claim no feel |
| Return to act | Avoidance | Avoidance in holy clothes |
| Repair if harm | No repair | No repair |

If your “regulation” means you never speak hard truth, it is fear — not mastery.

### 4) 5-day pause-before-act challenge

Before sharp reply, revenge spend, accusatory text, sexual compromise cue, or storm exit: run pause once.

| Day | Trigger | Named emotion | Pause? | Response chosen | Slip | Repair |
|-----|---------|---------------|--------|-----------------|------|--------|

### 5) Analogy: brake pedal

Speed without brakes is not freedom. Feeling without regulation is not authenticity. Riding the brake permanently is not wisdom — it is stall.

### 6) Better whole

Ask for help regulating (co-regulation as care). Do not outsource the brake permanently (“you calm me or I explode”). Course 11 + 07: first follower of your own rails.

### 7) Couples protocol

Either party may call a timed pause (10–20 min) with return time. Pause without return is abandonment. Return without ownership is theater.

### 8) Continuity into Week 3

Regulated people still meet conflict. Week 3 applies pause–name–repair when the bond heats.

### 9) Doctrine lock

Regulation does not manufacture teleios. It expresses Behavioral and Emotional stewardship of a teleios person under load. Success metrics: fewer ambushes, faster repair, clearer speech — not “I never feel intensely.”

---

### 11) Environment is part of the brake

Willpower-only regulation fails. Change cues:

- Phone out of bedroom
- Leave the room at volume spike
- Pre-written text you will not send for 20 minutes
- Walk loop before reply

Psychomotor and environment are not “cheating.” They are design-wise.

### 12) When the other refuses your pause

You still brake. You may say: “I’m pausing so I don’t harm; I’ll return at ____.” If they escalate, do not use their refusal as permission to explode. Your regulation is yours (better whole).

### 13) Load tiers — design the brake for each

| Load | What regulation looks like |
|------|----------------------------|
| Green | Short pause + name + continue conversation |
| Yellow | 10–20 min pause + return time |
| Red | Exit environment; no decisions; witness text; return next day for repair talk |

Pre-agree couple colors if bonded. Singles: pre-agree with yourself in writing so red days are not improvisation.

### 14) Linking regulation to Course 07 impulse log

Impulse peaks and emotion peaks often co-occur. One card can serve both: pause → name emotion → test desire/act against design → redirect. Do not run two competing systems that you will abandon.

### 15) Worked example — yellow load at home

Cue: spouse criticizes lateness; chest tight; premise “I’m never enough” (chase) tries to fire.

1. Call pause code; set return in 15 minutes.
2. Walk outside; breathe; name: shame + anger.
3. Rewrite premise: “I was late — act to own; I remain teleios.”
4. Return; own lateness; ask what would help; refuse contempt return fire.
5. Log; if you snapped anyway, repair same evening.

This is regulation as School 1 fruit — not a breathing aesthetic.

### 16) Measurement for the week

Success is not zero intensity. Success is: pause used ≥5 times, at least one return-time kept under yellow/red, one repaired slip, and a witness who heard you tell the truth about a failure. Without that evidence, retake the challenge before Week 3.
### 17) Premises that disable the brake

Catch these Mental premises before they cancel regulation:

- “If I pause, I lose.”
- “Real people don’t need brakes.”
- “This feeling must be discharged now or I’ll explode.”
- “They don’t deserve a regulated me.”

Rewrite each into a design premise. Unreformed premises make pause cards into wallpaper.

### 18) Body-first regulation (Psychomotor menu)

Pick two and practice cold (not only in fights):

- 90-second box breathing
- Walk to the end of the block and back
- Hands under cold water
- Sit on the floor; feet flat; name three objects you see

Body change often unlocks Mental rewrite. Ignoring the body is not “more spiritual.”

### 19) Evidence bar (raise it)

By Day 7 you should be able to show a witness: five pause logs, one red/yellow return-time kept, one repaired failure, and your pause card photo. No evidence → no Week 3 claim.

### 20) Linking to money, screens, and speech

Regulation is not only for marital tone. Pause before: send, spend, scroll, swear, storm out. Pick one non-relational domain this week and run the same card. Cross-training makes the brake reliable when the bond heats.

### 21) Final regulation charge

The brake is love's technique. Use it for the bond's good and your own Behavioral integrity. If you only regulate at work and explode at home, you have a compartment — not literacy. Close the compartment this week.

### 22) One-sentence doctrine

Regulation does not erase feeling; it refuses to let feeling write law for the mouth, the hands, or the household.

### 23) Teleios + better whole (regulation edition)

Regulation does not manufacture teleios. You brake because you are a teleios person responsible under load — not because a perfect streak will finally make you whole.

Better whole: co-regulation can be care; permanent outsourcing (“you calm me or I explode”) is fusion. First follower of your own pause card is you (Courses 07 / 11).

If chase returns (“I must feel calm to be acceptable”), rewrite: “I may feel intensely; I remain teleios; I choose the next governed act.”

### 24) Loop lock

Name (Week 1) without regulate (Week 2) is vocabulary for postmortems. Regulate without later conflict tools and repair leaves the Course 12 loop unfinished.

---

## Diagnostic — Regulation Audit

Score 1–5.

| Statement | Score |
|-----------|-------|
| Triggers mapped with premises | |
| Pause card written | |
| 5-day challenge logged honestly | |
| I replace reaction with response more often | |
| Brake is active, not numbness | |
| Freeze is not my fake peace | |
| Partner is not my only brake | |
| Return-times kept when pausing | |

---

## Case Contrasts

### Case A — No brake
Riley feels → harms → apologizes fog → repeats. Vocabulary from Week 1 unused at peak.

### Case B — Stuck brake
Avery never moves; calls silence peace; resentment ferments. Household pays.

### Case C — Active brake
Sam pauses, names fear, chooses one ask instead of contempt, logs five days, repairs one slip in hours.

---

## Seven-Day Drill

**Days 1–2:** Trigger map + pause card.  
**Days 3–7:** Pause-before-act challenge (5 days).  
Include at least one couple/family conflict if available.

---

---

## Course 01 parity — School 1 greatness evidence bar

Evidence: pause card used at least three times with log, brake → name → choose sequence on a red-load day, and refusal of freeze-as-virtue or flood-as-honesty in writing. Regulation that never reaches a chosen act is breathing aesthetic — not School 1 fruit.

### Integration — Courses 06–07 + 10

PD MasterClass and Self-Command installed Behavioral brakes. Course 10 conflict mastery assumes regulation before words. Week 2 is **governed emotion** — not suppressed emotion, not performed calm.

### Formation under load — Tuesday test
### Additional formation depth — Course 01 standard

School 1 greatness is not measured by reading completion. It is measured when a household can feel the rails: faster repair, cleaner speech, governed emotion, honored difference, and practice that starts from teleios rather than chasing worth. This week’s assignment must produce **observable fruit** — a log, a witness, a kept act, a retired phrase — not only insight.

Write one paragraph answering: *What would my closest relationship experience if I kept this week’s rule for 30 days?* If the answer is “nothing different,” the rule is too vague. Sharpen until the household would feel it.

Carry Course 01 integration forward: formation is structural; information is cosmetic. A great week leaves evidence in time, speech, and body — not only in notes.


Pause card in live conflict or sharp text temptation — not only in journaling. Literacy is public when covenant requires it.

## Reflection Questions

1. Where does reaction still win — and what payoff keeps it?
2. Is your “regulation” actually freeze?
3. What environmental change helps the brake (leave room, phone down)?
4. How does pause honor the other without fusion?
5. What failed pause taught you most?
6. How does Proverbs 16:32 confront your image of strength?

---

## Weekly Assignment

1. Regulation Audit  
2. Trigger sheet (top five)  
3. Pause practice card  
4. 5-day challenge log  
5. One repaired reaction write-up (exact sentences)  
6. Couples: written pause code word + return rule (or singles: personal pause rule with witness)

---

## Closing Declaration

> Feeling is not fate.  
> I brake, then choose.  
> Regulation bridges to action.  
> Honesty includes governance.  
> Chaos is not authenticity; numbness is not holiness.

---

## Outcome

You prove regulation with five days of pause-before-act — active control worthy of covenant life.
reflection_questions: Where does reaction still win?
Is your “regulation” actually freeze?
What cue needs environmental help (leave room)?
How does pause honor the other?
What failed pause taught you most?

modules.title: Emotion in Conflict
modules.content:
# Week 3: Emotion in Conflict
## Navigate the Storm — Tools, Not Denial

> **Week 3 of 4** | 8–10 hours | Conflict Emotions  
> **Sources:** Course 10 W5 · Course 09 W4 · Weeks 1–2 · Course 11 · better whole

---

## The Central Truth

Conflict exposes your emotional formation gaps.  
A storm at sea is navigable with tools — pause, name, repair — not with pretending the ocean is a pond, and not with baptizing blame weather as “honesty.” Literacy that fails in conflict was never literacy; it was classroom vocabulary.

---

## Week Overview

### Core Question
Which emotions run your conflict — and how do you steward them as a whole person?

### Key Insight
Top conflict emotions (anger, fear, shame, contempt, panic, humiliation) drive pattern more than the topic does. Practice pause–name–repair; replace blame with self-stewardship; journal three real conflict windows.

### Learning Outcomes
By the end of this week you will:

- Identify top two conflict emotions with stories and moves
- Install pause–name–repair as a spoken household/personal card
- Replace blame speech with stewardship speech in at least one live conflict
- Keep a 3-day (minimum) conflict emotion journal
- Pass an Emotion in Conflict Audit

---

## Core Teaching

### 1) Topic vs emotion captain

Most fights have a surface topic (dishes, money, tone, lateness) and an emotion captain (contempt, fear of abandonment, shame, envy). Master the captain or the topic forever returns.

### 2) Top two conflict emotions — map

For each:

| Field | Write |
|-------|-------|
| Emotion | |
| Typical cue | |
| Premise (Mental) | |
| Body | |
| Usual harmful move | |
| Design move | pause / name / ask / return-time / repair |

### 3) Pause — name — repair

1. **Pause** — Week 2 brake; set return time if exiting  
2. **Name** — emotion word aloud or on paper (Week 1)  
3. **Own** — your Behavioral move without fog  
4. **Repair** — ask + next act (Course 08 / 10)  

Sequence matters. Naming mid-explosion without pause is still discharge.

### 4) Blame → stewardship

| Blame | Stewardship |
|-------|-------------|
| You made me… | I felt X; I chose Y; I will Z |
| Always / never | This instance |
| Character attack | Act + impact |
| Scorekeeping | One rupture |

Blame protects ego. Stewardship protects design and bond.

### 5) Contempt special warning

Contempt is acid. If contempt is a top emotion, literacy requires naming it early and refusing contempt speech as “just how I talk.” Honor code (Course 09 W2) applies.

### 6) Conflict journal (3+ days)

| Conflict | Topic | Emotion captain | Named? | Pause? | Blame slipped? | Repair? | 24h trust |
|----------|-------|-----------------|--------|--------|----------------|---------|-----------|

### 7) Couples and singles

**Couples:** Use in live conflict with protocol from Course 10.  
**Singles:** Use in family/work/friend conflict — same literacy. Do not wait for marriage to learn navigation.

### 8) Analogy: storm at sea

Denial sinks ships. Panic without instruments sinks ships. Charts, compass, and practiced crew navigate. You are installing instruments.

### 9) Course 11 guard

Conflict shame (“I am a monster for feeling anger”) reinstalls chase. Anger can be named and governed; it is not proof you are non-teleios.

### 10) Continuity into Week 4

Even good navigation leaves tears in the fabric. Week 4 — emotional repair — is the proof of maturity.

---

### 11) Fear under anger (common captain swap)

Many “anger problems” are fear or shame wearing volume. Literacy asks: after pause, what second emotion appears? Name both. Repair both moves if both drove harm.

### 12) Singles: workplace and family as training ground

Do not postpone conflict literacy until marriage. A spat with a sibling or manager that you pause–name–repair is covenant rehearsal. Journal it with the same honesty.

### 13) Contempt detox micro-drill (3 days)

Each evening list any contempt word, joke, eye-roll, or “always/never” character attack you used. Rewrite each as: emotion named + act named + ask. Contempt is often unprocessed emotion + pride. Literacy refuses the costume.

### 14) When both captains fire

Two people, two emotion captains — e.g., their fear and your contempt. Protocol: sequential naming (one at a time), no dual monologues. First speaker gets mirror; then switch. Without sequence, you get parallel storms.

### 15) Worked example — money fight

Topic: overspend. Captains: your anxiety, their shame, mutual contempt risk.

Sequence: pause → you name anxiety without attacking character → they name shame without collapsing into shame ontology → each owns one Behavioral move → one budget next act → 24h trust read.

If contempt appears (“you’re so irresponsible”), stop topic; repair contempt first. Topic will wait; acid will not.

### 16) Week 3 evidence bar

Produce: two emotion maps, three journal rows, one blame→stewardship rewrite with before/after sentences, and one live conflict where pause–name–repair actually ran. Anything less is incomplete for a school that claims covenant formation.
### 17) The archive problem

Kitchen-sinking (bringing every past wound) is often unprocessed emotion captains wearing history as a weapon. Literacy rule: **one conflict window, one primary emotion captain, one topic.** Archives go to a scheduled repair talk — not to the peak.

### 18) Humor and “standards” as contempt costumes

Write three recent “jokes” or “I’m just saying” lines. For each: Was it play, or contempt with a smile? If contempt, rewrite as named emotion + clean ask. School 1 homes die by a thousand cute cuts.

### 19) Full worked sequence (anger over interrupted evening)

1. Cue: plans changed without consult.
2. Body: heat, jaw.
3. Illegal premise: “They never respect me” (always/never).
4. Pause code; 15-minute return.
5. Name: anger + beneath it, feeling dismissed.
6. Return: own any volume; ask for consult norm going forward.
7. Repair if contempt leaked.
8. Journal row same night.

Practice this sequence once from a real event this week — not a hypothetical.

### 20) Doctrine lock for conflict emotion

Feeling intensely in conflict does not make you immature. **Ungoverned** intensity that harms and won’t repair does. Teleios persons can feel fire and still keep the card.

### 21) After the fight — same-night micro-repair

Even if full repair talk waits until morning, same-night micro-repair is literacy:

> “I was flooding with ______; I owned ______ poorly; I will talk at ______ tomorrow; I am not abandoning.”

This prevents freeze-as-punishment and keeps return-time theology honest.

### 22) Final conflict-emotion charge

Your emotion captain will return. Literacy is not exile of feeling; it is governance under covenant weight. Keep the card on the fridge or phone lock screen. When contempt costumes appear, stop the topic and mend the acid first.

### 23) One-sentence doctrine

Conflict emotion is data under fire — name it, govern it, repair what it harmed, and refuse to crown it as captain of the bond.

### 24) Teleios + better whole (conflict edition)

Feeling fire in conflict does not mean you are non-teleios. Ungoverned harm that will not repair is the maturity failure — not the existence of anger, fear, or shame as feeling reports.

Better whole in the storm: you steward your emotion captain; you do not demand the other person permanently regulate you; you do not erase their agency with fusion (“we’re crazy”) or exile (“you’re the only storm”).

Course 11 guard: conflict shame that says “I am a monster for feeling” reinstalls chase. Name the feeling; own the act; keep the card.

### 25) Loop lock

Pause–name–repair in conflict is the third hinge of **name → regulate → conflict → repair**. Without Week 4 mend, navigation still leaves torn fabric.

---

## Diagnostic — Emotion in Conflict Audit

Score 1–5.

| Statement | Score |
|-----------|-------|
| Top two conflict emotions mapped | |
| Pause–name–repair card exists | |
| Practiced in live conflict | |
| Blame speech caught and rewritten | |
| Conflict journal done (≥3 entries) | |
| Contempt refused as style | |
| I refuse storm-denial | |
| Self-stewardship visible to a witness | |

---

## Case Contrasts

### Case A — Blame weather
Dana’s anger is always someone else’s fault. Naming never reaches her own move. Partner parents or flees.

### Case B — Silent storm
Morgan disappears; no name; returns as if nothing happened. Trust freezes.

### Case C — Navigation
Sam pauses, names fear under the anger, owns the raised voice, repairs with a next act, journals three conflicts, trust rises within 24 hours.

---

## Seven-Day Drill

**Day 1:** Top-two maps + card.  
**Days 2–4:** Conflict journal (seek real windows; do not pick fake fights).  
**Days 5–7:** Refine scripts; one blame→stewardship rewrite shared with witness.

---

---

## Course 01 parity — School 1 greatness evidence bar

Deliver: conflict captain map for two storms, blame → ownership rewrite, mid-storm naming once without fixing everything, and contempt-smile audit (three lines rewritten). Emotion in conflict without ownership is emotional intelligence cosplay — contempt with better vocabulary.

### Integration — Courses 09–10

Relatedness L2 and Mastery L3 supply protocol; Course 12 Week 3 supplies **emotion captaincy**. Better whole: name your part without fusion or exile language.

### Formation under load — Tuesday test
### Additional formation depth — Course 01 standard

School 1 greatness is not measured by reading completion. It is measured when a household can feel the rails: faster repair, cleaner speech, governed emotion, honored difference, and practice that starts from teleios rather than chasing worth. This week’s assignment must produce **observable fruit** — a log, a witness, a kept act, a retired phrase — not only insight.

Write one paragraph answering: *What would my closest relationship experience if I kept this week’s rule for 30 days?* If the answer is “nothing different,” the rule is too vague. Sharpen until the household would feel it.

Carry Course 01 integration forward: formation is structural; information is cosmetic. A great week leaves evidence in time, speech, and body — not only in notes.


One conflict where you named your emotion before assigning character verdicts. If you only name after victory, literacy is lagging — not leading.

## Reflection Questions

1. Which conflict emotion is your captain?
2. Where does blame protect you from ownership?
3. What happens when you name mid-storm after a pause?
4. How does this serve covenant readiness if you are unmarried?
5. What journal line surprised you?
6. Where does contempt still disguise as humor or “standards”?

---

## Weekly Assignment

1. Emotion in Conflict Audit  
2. Top-two emotion maps  
3. Pause–name–repair card (shared if coupled)  
4. Conflict journal (≥3 entries)  
5. One blame→stewardship rewrite (before/after sentences)  
6. 400–600 words: “My emotion captain in conflict”

---

## Closing Declaration

> Conflict exposes gaps.  
> I pause, name, and repair.  
> Blame ends; stewardship begins.  
> Storms are navigable.  
> I refuse contempt and denial.

---

## Outcome

You steward conflict emotions with tools — not denial, not blame weather — as literacy under fire.
reflection_questions: Which conflict emotion is your captain?
Where does blame protect you from ownership?
What happens when you name mid-storm?
How does this serve covenant readiness?
What journal line surprised you?

modules.title: Emotional Repair
modules.content:
# Week 4: Emotional Repair
## Mend the Fabric — Restore Capacity

> **Week 4 of 4** | 9–11 hours | Capstone  
> **Sources:** Course 08 W4 · Course 10 W6 · Weeks 1–3 · Course 11 · Matthew 5:23–24

---

## The Central Truth

Repair is the final proof of emotional maturity.  
Mending fabric restores usefulness; ignoring tears guarantees failure under load. Emotional literacy that ends in vocabulary certificates without mended relationships is unfinished. Maturity is evidenced in the mend — as a teleios person who owns acts without identity deletion.

---

## Week Overview

### Core Question
What makes emotional repair land — for couples and singles?

### Key Insight
Autopsy last two repair attempts; build an emotional repair ritual that includes naming; practice live with a trusted person; write a Course 12 closing charter that carries into Temperament Intelligence without contempt.

### Learning Outcomes
By the end of this week you will:

- Autopsy two emotional repair attempts with 48-hour trust read
- Write an emotional repair ritual (name → own → ask → next act)
- Practice the ritual live once this week
- Distinguish repair from self-erasure and from gift-bribery
- Complete Emotional Literacy closing charter

---

## Core Teaching

### 1) Why repair is the proof

Naming and regulation can be private. Repair is public to the bond. Hebrews-shaped maturity (responsibility under load) shows when torn relatedness is restored by truth.

Matthew 5:23–24: reconciliation priority over religious performance — repair is not optional polish.

### 2) Autopsy template (two attempts)

For each:

- Emotion involved (Week 1 word)  
- What I said/did  
- What I avoided naming  
- What the other needed  
- Self-erasure or fog?  
- Next act kept?  
- Trust at 48 hours (up / flat / down)  

Patterns teach more than intentions.

### 3) Emotional repair ritual

1. Request a repair talk (or scheduled window)  
2. Name the emotion you discharged poorly  
3. Name the act and impact (specific)  
4. Own without fog (“I did…”)  
5. Paraphrase their impact if they share  
6. Ask what would help  
7. One next regulated act + time  
8. Log follow-through 7 days  
9. Do not demand instant “it’s fine” feelings  

### 4) Repair ≠ self-erasure ≠ bribery

| Real repair | Self-erasure | Bribery |
|-------------|--------------|---------|
| Own act | “I’m trash; parent me” | Gift without ownership |
| Next rail | Endless apology fog | Distraction |
| Honor both | Fusion | Avoidance |

Course 11: conviction, not shame ontology, inside the apology.

### 5) Forgiveness vs trust (recall)

Forgiveness may release revenge debt; trust rebuilds by bricks (Course 09–10). Emotional repair can start both — it does not force premature “I trust you.”

### 6) Analogy: mending fabric

Stitched cloth carries weight again. Unmended tears spread under the next load. Pretty patches that skip the stitch (fog apologies) fail at the seam.

### 7) Couples and singles

**Couples:** Practice with spouse; use governance meeting if stuck (Course 09 W6).  
**Singles:** Practice with family/friend you actually ruptured with — literacy is not theoretical.

### 8) Integration — Course 12 loop

Name → Regulate → Conflict tools → Repair.  
Remove repair and the loop is unfinished School 1 work.

### 9) Continuity into Course 13

Temperament differences will tempt contempt (“they’re too much / too cold”). Emotional repair skills + Course 11 ontology prepare you to honor difference without resentment museums.

### 10) Final ratiocination

- Premise 1: Finite persons rupture emotionally.
- Premise 2: Unrepaired emotional rupture compounds into contempt or distance.
- Premise 3: Named, owned, followed-through repair restores capacity without erasing persons.
- Conclusion: Emotional repair is literacy’s capstone — or literacy was theater.

---

### 11) Repair scripts (adapt; do not recite robotically)

> “I felt ______ and I discharged it by ______. That impacted you by ______. I own that. What would help? My next act is ______ by ______.”

If they are not ready to talk: deliver ownership + next act in writing, invite a time, do not demand absolution.

### 12) When repair is refused

You still own and change. Forgiveness is theirs to give; your Behavioral next act is yours. Do not use their refusal as excuse to return to contempt. Wisdom may add boundaries (Course 09).

### 13) 48-hour trust read (how to score)

After repair: Did they initiate warmth? Did you keep the next act? Did conflict residual stay or clear? Score trust up/flat/down without demanding they perform forgiveness feelings on your timeline.

### 14) Capstone standard for School 1

A School 1 graduate can: name emotion, brake, navigate conflict emotion, and mend. If any leg is missing, the “great school” claim fails in the kitchen. Your charter must name which leg is still weakest and the 30-day rail for it.

### 15) Repair and the four faculties (integration)

A complete emotional repair often needs:

- **Cognitive** — accurate account of what happened
- **Mental** — reject “I am trash” / “they are trash”
- **Emotional** — name what was discharged
- **Affective** — care about impact without fusion
- **Conative** — commit to next act
- **Psychomotor** — show up for the talk; posture; eye contact
- **Behavioral** — keep the next act

Missing faculties produce fog apologies or technical non-human repairs.

### 16) When you are the injured party

Literacy is not only apologizing. If you were harmed:

1. Name your emotion without character assassination
2. State the impact
3. State what would help (boundary, act, time)
4. Refuse moving goalposts as revenge (Course 09)
5. Distinguish forgiveness process from trust bricks

Better whole: you may require structure without becoming a permanent prosecutor.

### 17) Closing charter checklist (Course 12)

Must include: lexicon growth proof, pause card, conflict captain maps, repair ritual, weakest leg + 30-day rail, Course 11 teleios sentences preserved. If chase or feeling-as-ontology returned, confess it in the charter.

### 18) School 1 greatness test

Can your household feel safer because you can mend? If not, literacy is still academic. Mend once more before you collect the certificate in your heart.

### 19) Gift, touch, and timing

Restitution may include a gift or act of service — **after** ownership, never instead of it. Touch may comfort — never coerce forgiveness. Timing: do not force a repair talk at peak red load; schedule it; keep the schedule. Structure is love’s body language.

### 20) Final repair charge

Mend once more than you prefer. Prefer structure over relief. Prefer ownership over fog. Prefer next acts over speeches. Then walk into Course 13 able to honor difference without using emotional illiteracy as an excuse for contempt.

### 21) One-sentence doctrine

Emotional maturity is not a calm personality; it is the practiced power to mend what ungoverned feeling tore.

### 22) Teleios + better whole (repair edition)

You mend as a teleios person who wounded in practice — not as someone inventing worth through apology theater, and not as someone deleting identity (“I’m trash; parent me”).

Better whole: a partner may forgive and help; a partner is not your permanent conscience chip or emotional completeness. Repair restores relatedness between whole persons; it does not assemble half-selves.

Course 11 grammar inside the apology: conviction about the act, not shame-as-ontology.

### 23) Loop complete

**Name → regulate → conflict tools → repair.** This week closes the loop. Remove mend and Course 12 was vocabulary certificates. Carry the ritual into Course 13 without using temperament difference as an excuse for unrepaired contempt.

---

## Diagnostic — Emotional Repair Audit

Score 1–5.

| Statement | Score |
|-----------|-------|
| Two attempts autopsied | |
| Ritual written | |
| Practiced live this week | |
| Repair includes emotion naming | |
| I refuse gift-bribe without ownership | |
| I refuse self-erasure apologies | |
| Follow-through logged | |
| Closing charter holds Course 11 grammar | |

---

## Case Contrasts

### Case A — Skip mend
Drew waits for “time.” Time without stitch widens the tear. Fine culture returns.

### Case B — Over-apologize fog
Avery collapses into “I’m the worst”; other person parents; no next act. Temporary calm; no structure.

### Case C — Mend
Sam names the discharged contempt, owns the words, asks what would help, offers a Week 2 pause code in future fights, logs seven days; trust rises.

---

## Seven-Day Drill — Capstone

**Days 1–2:** Autopsy + ritual draft.  
**Days 3–5:** Live practice + follow-through start.  
**Days 6–7:** Closing charter; witness review.

---

---

## Course 01 parity — School 1 greatness evidence bar

Capstone evidence: two repair autopsies, live ritual practiced, 48-hour trust read honest, closing charter 700–1000 words with weakest leg + 30-day rail. Emotional repair skipped means Course 12 failed the kitchen test — certificates notwithstanding.

### Integration — Course 13 + full School 1

Course 13 temperament honor requires mend capacity — contempt grows in unmended tears. Week 4 closes **name → regulate → conflict → repair**. Course 01 parity: maturity is capacity evidenced under load.

### Formation under load — Tuesday test
### Additional formation depth — Course 01 standard

School 1 greatness is not measured by reading completion. It is measured when a household can feel the rails: faster repair, cleaner speech, governed emotion, honored difference, and practice that starts from teleios rather than chasing worth. This week’s assignment must produce **observable fruit** — a log, a witness, a kept act, a retired phrase — not only insight.

Write one paragraph answering: *What would my closest relationship experience if I kept this week’s rule for 30 days?* If the answer is “nothing different,” the rule is too vague. Sharpen until the household would feel it.

Carry Course 01 integration forward: formation is structural; information is cosmetic. A great week leaves evidence in time, speech, and body — not only in notes.


Mend once more than comfort prefers this week. Structure over relief; ownership over fog.

## Reflection Questions

1. Which repair failure repeats across years?
2. What emotion do you still refuse to name inside apology?
3. How does mending differ from self-erasure?
4. What will you carry into temperament work?
5. What proves literacy in your household this month — observable?
6. Where have you demanded forgiveness feelings on your timeline?

---

## Weekly Assignment

1. Emotional Repair Audit  
2. Two-attempt autopsy  
3. Written emotional repair ritual  
4. Live practice write-up + 7-day follow-through plan  
5. Course 12 closing charter (700–1000 words) integrating name/regulate/conflict/repair and Course 11 teleios grammar  
6. One gratitude note to the person who received your repair

---

## Closing Declaration

> Repair proves literacy.  
> I mend what I tear.  
> Emotions named, governed, repaired.  
> Covenant life requires this fabric whole.  
> I am teleios — I steward feeling without worshiping it.

---

## Outcome

You complete Course 12 with a live emotional repair ritual — maturity evidenced in the mend, ready for temperament honor without contempt.
reflection_questions: Which repair failure repeats?
What emotion do you still refuse to name in apology?
How does mending differ from self-erasure?
What will you carry into temperament work?
What proves literacy in your household this month?

modules.content:
# Week 1: Temperament Basics
## Palette Colors — Understand, Don’t Judge

> **Week 1 of 3** | 8–10 hours | Temperamental Attribute  
> **Sources:** Course 02 Week 3 Attributes · Course 06 W5 · Course 11–12 · better whole

---

## The Central Truth

Temperament is the energy and flavor of a person; it must be **understood, not judged**.  
Colors on a palette differ; the painting needs more than one. Misreading temperament as character defect breeds contempt. Using temperament as an excuse for harm breeds chaos. School 1 ends here only if both errors die.

Temperament is the **Temperamental attribute** — not ontology, not destiny, not a free pass.

---

## Week Overview

### Core Question
How do we describe temperament without ontology baptism or excuse theology?

### Key Insight
Sketch descriptive axes (pace, intensity, sociability, structure preference, conflict approach); list strengths and limits; rewrite one misread of spouse or close other; log five days under load.

### Learning Outcomes
By the end of this week you will:

- Locate temperament inside the Attributes map (not Faculties collapse)
- Sketch your profile and one other person’s profile descriptively
- List strengths and limits for both without contempt words
- Rewrite one misinterpretation (“lazy/cold/dramatic/controlling”) into temperament + stewardship ask
- Complete a 5-day temperament reflection log
- Pass a Temperament Basics Audit

---

## Core Teaching

### 1) Where temperament sits (doctrine lock)

**Attributes (Course 02):** Behavioral · Temperamental · Emotional · Mental  

**Faculties (Course 04):** Conative · Cognitive · Psychomotor · Affective  

Temperament is **not** Cognitive faculty and not Emotional attribute — though it interacts with both. Do not say “my temperament made me think X” when you mean a Mental premise you still own. Do not say “temperament” when you mean ungoverned emotion (Course 12).

### 2) Descriptive axes (not rigid boxes)

Sketch yourself and the other on:

- Pace (fast ↔ slow)  
- Intensity (high ↔ low)  
- Sociability (outward ↔ reserved)  
- Structure preference (planned ↔ flexible)  
- Conflict approach (engage fast ↔ process then speak)  
- Recovery need (quick bounce ↔ longer quiet)  

Blends are normal. Primary under fatigue matters most.

### 3) Strengths and limits (both required)

| Flavor lean | Strength gift | Limit risk if unstewarded |
|-------------|---------------|---------------------------|
| Fast pace | Initiative | Impatience, steamroll |
| Slow pace | Depth, caution | Delay, withdrawal read as rejection |
| High intensity | Passion, clarity | Overwhelm, volume |
| Low intensity | Calm | Under-response read as indifference |
| Reserved | Depth, loyalty | Stonewall risk |
| Outward | Warmth, connection | Oversharing, intrusion |

Neither column is teleios vs un-teleios. Stewardship is.

### 4) Misinterpretation inventory

Common contempt translations:

- Slow → “lazy”  
- Fast → “controlling”  
- Reserved → “cold”  
- Intense → “crazy/dramatic”  
- Flexible → “irresponsible”  
- Structured → “rigid/joyless”  

Rewrite one:

> Old story: ______  
> Temperament read: ______  
> Stewardship ask (clean): ______  
> What I will stop calling it: ______

### 5) Not an excuse (Course 06 W5 continuity)

Temperament explains *tendency*. It does not authorize:

- broken vows  
- contempt  
- abandonment without return  
- cruelty  
- refusal to repair  

“That’s just my temperament” after harm is excuse theology. Teleios persons steward attributes.

### 6) 5-day reflection log

| Day | My flavor under load | Their flavor | Misread risk | Honor act | Excuse temptation? |
|-----|----------------------|--------------|--------------|-----------|--------------------|

### 7) Analogy: palette

Judge the painting’s harmony, not a single pigment as “wrong for existing.” You may still ask a color to be applied with skill — that is stewardship, not erasure.

### 8) Better whole

Do not demand your spouse become your temperament. Harmony is coordinated wholes (Week 3), not cloning.

### 9) Married focus; singles transferable

Course title centers marriage; the literacy transfers to family and close bonds. Unmarried learners: practice on a real close relationship now — do not wait to disrespect a future spouse’s flavor.

### 10) Continuity into Week 2

Basics without conflict application remain theory. Week 2: temperament in conflict — curiosity over defect theology.

---

### 11) Working sketch — two columns (fill honestly)

**Me under fatigue:** pace __ · intensity __ · sociability __ · structure __ · conflict __ · recovery __  
**Them under fatigue:** (same)

Then circle the axis most likely to generate contempt words in your mouth this month. That axis is your Week 1 priority honor field.

### 12) Church / culture misreads

Temperament contempt is not only marital. “Real leaders are loud.” “Spiritual people are always gentle-paced.” Test those slogans against design: gifts differ; holiness does not require one flavor.

### 13) Extended case — “lazy” rewrite

Old: “You never help; you’re lazy.”  
Temperament: slow pace + reserved recovery after work.  
Truth mix: sometimes also Behavioral neglect — hold both.  
Stewardship ask: “I need thirty minutes of shared chores starting at 7:30; do you want a buffer after work first?”  
Honor: thank the depth they bring when they are not rushed.  
Refuse: using “temperament” to dodge the chore — and using “lazy” to erase their flavor.

### 14) Self-profile honesty check

Have a witness guess your fatigue profile. Where their guess differs from yours, investigate. Self-flattery (“I’m intense in a good way only”) is as dangerous as contempt for the other.

### 15) Interaction with other attributes (precision)

- Temperament × **Mental**: fast minds may leap to premises; slow minds may over-qualify. Both still own premises.
- Temperament × **Emotional**: intensity flavor is not the same as Emotional surge — but they amplify each other.
- Temperament × **Behavioral**: pace shows in habits; still no excuse for broken rails.
- Temperament × **faculties**: a reserved person still has Affective capacity; quiet ≠ uncaring.

Wrong collapses create false compassion or false condemnation.

### 16) Spouse interview (30 minutes) — if married / partnered

Ask (without defending):

1. What word do you fear I use for your flavor?
2. When do you feel steamrolled or abandoned by my pace?
3. What strength of yours do I under-thank?
4. What clean ask would help this month?

Singles: ask a close family member or friend the same about your flavor in conflict.

### 17) Vocabulary forbid list (start now)

Write five contempt words you will not use about their temperament (lazy, crazy, cold, dramatic, controlling, clingy, etc.). Post them. Week 2–3 will test the list.

### 18) Strengths you must stop resenting

List three strengths in the other that cost you comfort (their social energy, their caution, their drive). Resentment of a gift is a heart issue, not a temperament insight. Convert each into one honor sentence and one clean ask if a downside exists.

### 19) Final basics charge

If you finish Week 1 still using one contempt word on your forbid list, you have incomplete basics. Retire the word in speech for seven days and log every catch. Understanding without mouth discipline is not intelligence.

### 20) One-sentence doctrine

Temperament is flavor to understand and steward — never a verdict on worth, never a license to harm, never a reason for contempt.

## Diagnostic — Temperament Basics Audit

Score 1–5.

| Statement | Score |
|-----------|-------|
| Temperament located in Attributes map correctly | |
| Two profiles sketched | |
| Strengths and limits listed without contempt | |
| One misread rewritten | |
| 5-day log completed | |
| I refuse temperament-as-excuse | |
| I refuse temperament-as-contempt target | |
| Better whole explicit (no clone demand) | |

---

## Case Contrasts

### Case A — Contempt reader
Dana calls slow “lazy,” reserved “cold,” and builds a museum of injuries. Difference becomes moral defect. Marriage climate: contempt.

### Case B — Excuse artist
Riley harms, delays repair, blames “my temperament.” Attribute used as free pass. Climate: chaos with psychology vocabulary.

### Case C — Palette literacy
Sam sketches both profiles, rewrites one misread, logs five days, honors a strength daily, still owns Behavioral misses without excuse.

---

## Seven-Day Drill

**Days 1–2:** Profiles + strengths/limits + misread rewrite.  
**Days 3–7:** Reflection log (5 days minimum inside the week).

---

---

## Course 01 parity — School 1 greatness evidence bar

Produce: two axis profiles, misread rewrite delivered aloud, five-day log, forbid list posted with seven-day zero-use or catch-and-repair log. Temperament basics without mouth discipline is psychology tourism — not School 1 finale prep.

### Integration — Course 06 W5 + Course 02

Temperamental attribute was named in Course 02 and trained in MasterClass Week 5. Course 13 completes **honor without clone demand**. Attributes ≠ Faculties — do not collapse temperament into Cognitive or Emotional excuses.

### Formation under load — Tuesday test
### Additional formation depth — Course 01 standard

School 1 greatness is not measured by reading completion. It is measured when a household can feel the rails: faster repair, cleaner speech, governed emotion, honored difference, and practice that starts from teleios rather than chasing worth. This week’s assignment must produce **observable fruit** — a log, a witness, a kept act, a retired phrase — not only insight.

Write one paragraph answering: *What would my closest relationship experience if I kept this week’s rule for 30 days?* If the answer is “nothing different,” the rule is too vague. Sharpen until the household would feel it.

Carry Course 01 integration forward: formation is structural; information is cosmetic. A great week leaves evidence in time, speech, and body — not only in notes.


Honor act on a day their flavor irritates you most. Understanding without honor is contempt with notes.

### Parity seal

This week meets Course 01 depth when your witness can describe one visible change in your speech, schedule, or repair — without you prompting them. If they cannot, extend the week. School 1 does not graduate fog. Keep the evidence visible for ninety days. Honor daily.

## Reflection Questions

1. What contempt word do you use for their flavor?
2. Where do you excuse yourself with temperament?
3. What strength of theirs have you refused to honor?
4. How does better whole change “make them like me”?
5. What did the log show under fatigue that calm days hid?
6. Where have you collapsed temperament into Emotional or Mental wrongly?

---

## Weekly Assignment

1. Temperament Basics Audit  
2. Two profile sketches (axes)  
3. Strengths/limits tables  
4. Misread rewrite sheet  
5. 5-day reflection log  
6. 400–600 words: “What I was calling a character defect”

---

## Closing Declaration

> Temperament is flavor, not fate.  
> I understand before I judge.  
> No excuse; no contempt.  
> Palette — many colors, one design honor.  
> I steward my attribute; I honor theirs.

---

## Outcome

You hold descriptive profiles and a rewritten misread — temperament literacy without judgment theater or excuse theology.
reflection_questions: What contempt word do you use for their flavor?
Where do you excuse yourself with temperament?
What strength of theirs have you refused to honor?
How does better whole change “make them like me”?
What did the log show under fatigue?

modules.title: Temperament in Conflict
modules.content:
# Week 2: Temperament in Conflict
## Different Notes — Not Character Defects

> **Week 2 of 3** | 8–10 hours | Conflict Under Flavor Clash  
> **Sources:** Week 1 · Course 10 W5 · Course 12 W3 · Course 09 W4 · better whole

---

## The Central Truth

Conflict often reveals **temperament differences**, not character defects.  
Musical notes clash until arranged; curiosity arranges better than judgment. Defect theology (“they’re broken for being slow/fast/intense/quiet”) is contempt with a moral costume. Endless analysis without decision is also failure — curiosity is a tool, not a hiding place.

---

## Week Overview

### Core Question
How do we govern temperament clash without contempt and without excuse?

### Key Insight
List two recurring conflicts tied to temperament; pause and ask before reacting; replace judgment with curiosity; still use conflict protocol (own, repair); journal three days.

### Learning Outcomes
By the end of this week you will:

- Name two recurring conflicts as flavor-clash + topic
- Install pause-and-ask before defect-labeling
- Practice curiosity scripts that still lead to decisions
- Keep a 3-day temperament conflict journal
- Pass a Temperament in Conflict Audit

---

## Core Teaching

### 1) Two layers of a fight

1. **Topic** — money, chores, sex timing, in-laws, punctuality  
2. **Flavor clash** — fast closer vs slow processor; engagers vs withdrawers; high intensity vs low  

If you only fight the topic, the clash returns dressed as a new topic.

### 2) Two recurring conflicts — map

For each:

| Field | Write |
|-------|-------|
| Topic | |
| My flavor move | |
| Their flavor move | |
| Contempt story I tell | |
| Defect label I reach for | |
| Curious question | |
| Clean stewardship ask | |
| Protocol step (Course 10) | |

### 3) Pause and ask (temperament edition)

Before reacting:

1. Brake (Course 12 / 07)  
2. Ask internally: “Defect — or different pace/intensity?”  
3. Ask aloud one curious question  
4. Then own your move and use conflict card  

Curiosity that never reaches a decision is avoidance. Time-box: curiosity → decision window.

### 4) Curiosity scripts (examples — write yours)

- “Help me understand what you need when you’re quiet.”  
- “I move fast; do you need twenty minutes before we decide?”  
- “My intensity is up; is volume the problem or the content?”  
- “I’m not withdrawing to punish — I need a return time. I’ll be back at ____.”  

### 5) Judgment → curiosity → still responsibility

| Judgment | Curiosity | Responsibility |
|----------|-----------|----------------|
| You’re cold | What’s your processing need? | I will not stonewall without return |
| You’re controlling | What’s your pace fear? | I will not steamroll deadlines of care |
| You’re dramatic | What’s the intensity signal? | I will not use volume as dominance |

### 6) Journal (3 days)

| Conflict | Flavors | Judgment thought | Curious ask | Decision made? | Outcome |
|----------|---------|------------------|-------------|----------------|---------|

### 7) Analogy: musical notes

Dissonance can resolve to harmony. Contempt is refusing to read the score. Walking off stage mid-piece without return time is not “temperament” — it is ungoverned Behavioral exit.

### 8) Power and temperament (Course 09 W3)

The faster / louder / more socially skilled person can “win” conflicts while losing the bond. Submit power to protocol. The slower processor needs voice without being labeled defective.

### 9) Course 11–12 guards

- Do not shame yourself for having a flavor (“I am broken for being intense”).  
- Do not dump unregulated emotion and call it “my fiery temperament.”  
- Name emotion (Course 12) *and* read temperament (this course).

### 10) Continuity into Week 3

Curiosity prepares daily honor. Week 3: harmony challenge — appreciation list, honor acts, complaint→gratitude, School 1 closing.

---

### 11) Pursue–withdraw with temperament glasses

Often pursue = higher intensity / faster pace; withdraw = reserved / slow processor. Protocol: withdrawer sets return time; pursuer journals one ask; both refuse defect labels (“needy” / “cold”) during the pause.

### 12) Sexual timing conflicts (marriage)

Pace and intensity differences often surface sexually. Honor means: no coercion, no contempt for desire level differences, clean asks, Course 06 W11 loyalty. Difference is not defect; pressure is not intimacy (Course 10 W7).

### 13) Decision time-box template

Curiosity window: 15 minutes.  
Then: one decision, or one scheduled decision time within 24 hours.  
Write the decision.  
If slow processor needs more time: agree the deadline now — not infinite delay.

This keeps Week 2 from becoming endless soft conflict.

### 14) In-law / extended family flavor clashes

Temperament contempt often enters through family of origin stories (“in our family we just say it”). Translate: different intensity norms. Honor your spouse’s flavor in front of your family. Public contempt of your spouse’s temperament is covenant betrayal with manners.

### 15) Full map — conflict #1 and #2 (force specificity)

Reproduce this twice in your notes:

**Conflict title:** ______  
**Last date it happened:** ______  
**Topic surface:** ______  
**My fatigue flavor:** ______  
**Their fatigue flavor:** ______  
**My contempt word:** ______  
**Their likely wound story:** ______  
**Curious question I will actually ask:** ______  
**Decision time-box:** ______  
**Repair if I used contempt:** ______

Vague maps produce vague marriages.

### 16) The “spiritualized preference” problem

Sometimes we baptize our temperament as the godly one (“gentle always waits”; “leaders always push”). Test preferences against design fruit: truth, fidelity, honor, repair. Preferring your own flavor is normal; sacralizing it is pride.

### 17) Practice drill — 72-hour curiosity

In the next 72 hours, during one real friction:

1. Pause
2. Ask one curious question from your card
3. Time-box a decision
4. Own your flavor move
5. Journal the row

If you avoid all friction to protect the assignment, you fail the assignment.

### 18) Doctrine lock

Difference is not defect. Difference is also not destiny. Teleios persons with different temperaments still keep covenants, tell truth, and repair. Curiosity serves responsibility — it does not replace it.

### 19) Extended case — bedtime clash

Fast closer wants lights out decision now; slow processor needs twenty minutes. Contempt scripts: “You’re a child” / “You’re a dictator.”  
Design play: curious ask + time-box (“twenty minutes, then we decide”) + no volume dominance + morning review if it failed.  
Journal it once this week even if bedtime is not your issue — use your real analogue (leaving parties, ending visits, closing purchases).

### 20) What “mastery” means here

Not never clashing. Mastery is: shorter contempt half-life, faster curiosity, kept time-boxes, repaired defect-labels same day. Measure that — not vibes.

### 21) Final conflict charge

Curiosity without decision breeds fog. Decision without curiosity breeds tyranny. Hold both. Time-box. Repair defect labels same day. That is temperament intelligence under fire — worthy of a great school.

### 22) One-sentence doctrine

In conflict, curiosity opens the door and responsibility walks through it — on time.

### 23) School 1 greatness evidence bar

By week’s end you must show: two conflict maps with teleios lines intact, one curiosity question asked live, one time-boxed decision kept, and one same-day repair of a defect-label. Without that evidence, temperament talk remains theory — not School 1 fruit.

## Diagnostic — Temperament in Conflict Audit

Score 1–5.

| Statement | Score |
|-----------|-------|
| Two conflicts mapped as flavor + topic | |
| Pause-and-ask practiced | |
| Judgment→curiosity at least twice | |
| Decisions still reached (no endless analysis) | |
| 3-day journal done | |
| Defect-labeling refused | |
| Protocol still used | |
| Power submitted to the card | |

---

## Case Contrasts

### Case A — Defect theology
Avery moralizes pace differences; every fight becomes character court. Curiosity absent. Contempt climate.

### Case B — Endless analysis
Morgan “understands temperament” forever and never decides bedtime, budget, or repair. Hiding in psychology talk.

### Case C — Curious skill
Sam pauses, asks, time-boxes a decision, owns steamroll or withdrawal, repairs, journals three clashes; harmony begins.

---

## Seven-Day Drill

**Day 1:** Two conflict maps + curiosity scripts.  
**Days 2–4:** Journal live conflicts.  
**Days 5–7:** One repaired contempt moment; refine scripts.

---

---

## Course 01 parity — School 1 greatness evidence bar

Evidence: two conflict maps with teleios lines intact, curiosity question asked live, time-boxed decision kept, same-day repair if you defect-labeled. Temperament in conflict without protocol is analysis paralysis or contempt — both fail School 1.

### Integration — Courses 10 + 12

Conflict mastery (Course 10) and emotional literacy (Course 12) meet **flavor clash** here. Curiosity is tool, not hiding place — decision window required. Better whole: different notes, not character defects.

### Formation under load — Tuesday test
### Additional formation depth — Course 01 standard

School 1 greatness is not measured by reading completion. It is measured when a household can feel the rails: faster repair, cleaner speech, governed emotion, honored difference, and practice that starts from teleios rather than chasing worth.
